## Data Analysis and Investigations on Mortality Rates in Scotland due to Coronary Heart Disease

---

class: inverse, center, middle

## Problem Statement 1: 
What is the trend in mortality rates of each gender due to coronary heart disease for those over 75 years old from 2015-2023?
---
#Tidying Data
--
```{r}
#Selecting necessary columns from the dataset

hd_mortality <- hd_mortalitybyca [, c("Year", "AgeGroup", "Sex", "Diagnosis", "NumberOfDeaths", "CrudeRate", "Ca")]

```
--
```{r}
#Filtering and tidying the specific data

hd_mortality_year <- hd_mortality %>% 
  filter(
  Year != "2024p", 
  Ca == "S92000003",
  Diagnosis == "Coronary Heart Disease",
  AgeGroup %in% c("75plus years"),
  Sex != "All") %>%
    mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year)) %>%
  arrange(Sex)
```
---
```{r}
hd_mortality_year
```
---

# Codes
```{r}
#Creating linear regression models
mortality_female_fit <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(CrudeRate ~ Year, 
      data = hd_mortality_year %>% filter(Sex == "Female")) 

mortality_male_fit <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(CrudeRate ~ Year, 
      data = hd_mortality_year %>% filter(Sex == "Male")) 
```
---
```{r}
mortality_male_fit
```

```{r}
mortality_female_fit
```
---
```{r}
mortality_female_aug <- augment(mortality_female_fit$fit) %>%
                                mutate(Sex = "Female")

mortality_male_aug <- augment(mortality_male_fit$fit) %>%
                                mutate(Sex = "Male")

mortality_year_fit_aug <- bind_rows(
  mortality_female_aug,
  mortality_male_aug
) %>%
  mutate(residual = ifelse(.resid >0, TRUE, FALSE))
```

---
# Plots
```{r recode-species, echo = FALSE}
ggplot(data = mortality_year_fit_aug) + 
 geom_point(aes(x = Year, y = CrudeRate, color = residual)) +
  geom_line(aes(x = Year, y = .fitted), linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = Year,y = .fitted), color = "purple")+
  geom_segment(mapping = aes(x = Year, y = CrudeRate,
                             xend = Year, yend = .fitted), color = "purple", alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Coronary Heart Disease Mortality Rates in Scotland (2015-2023)",
    subtitle = "For ages 75 years and above",
    x = "Year (2015-2023)",
    y = "Crude Rate (per 100,000 population)",
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Sex, scales = "free_y", axes = "all") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("hotpink", "forestgreen"))
```

## Problem Statement 2: 
Identifying which areas have seen the largest and smallest changes, and whether any areas have seen no improvement, to show where progress has been uneven. 
---

#Tidying Data 
```{r}
# Filtering for 2015 data 
hd_total2015 <- hd_mortalitybyca %>% 
  filter(Year == 2015, 
         AgeGroup == "All Ages", 
         Sex == "All",
         Diagnosis == "Coronary Heart Disease")
```
--
```{r}
#Finding out the national rate 
scotland_rate <- hd_total2015 %>% 
  filter(Ca == "S92000003") %>% 
  pull(CrudeRate) 
```
---
```{r}
#Identifying whether it is above or below the national rate  
hd_councils <- hd_total2015 %>% 
  filter(Diagnosis == "Coronary Heart Disease", Ca != "S92000003") %>%
  mutate(national_rate = scotland_rate,
         difference = CrudeRate - national_rate, 
         status = if_else(CrudeRate > national_rate, "Above national", "Below national")) 

council_area_rate <- hd_councils %>% 
  select(national_rate, difference, status, Ca) 

glimpse(council_area_rate) 

```
